note: SAMPLE breed profiles for the Pet Finder demo. General guidance only; check with a vet before relying on it.

Doberman.summary: A sleek, athletic and loyal dog, often kept as a guard dog and family companion.
Doberman.goodToKnow: Alert and protective; best with an experienced owner

Golden Retriever.summary: A friendly, gentle and eager-to-please dog, popular with families.
Golden Retriever.needs: Daily walks, play and regular brushing
Golden Retriever.goodToKnow: Good with children; sheds a lot of hair

Egyptian Mau.summary: A naturally spotted, fast and active cat that bonds closely with its family.
Egyptian Mau.needs: Daily play, climbing spaces and attention
Egyptian Mau.goodToKnow: Can be shy with strangers at first

British Shorthair.summary: A calm, sturdy cat with a thick, plush coat and an easy-going nature.
British Shorthair.needs: Weekly brushing and gentle daily play
British Shorthair.goodToKnow: Gains weight easily, so watch its food

Mini Lop.summary: A small, friendly rabbit with floppy ears that enjoys gentle handling.
Mini Lop.needs: Fresh hay, space to hop and daily company
Mini Lop.goodToKnow: Needs a cool, shaded spot in hot weather

New Zealand White.summary: A large, calm white rabbit kept both as a pet and for meat.
New Zealand White.needs: Fresh hay, a roomy hutch and shade
New Zealand White.goodToKnow: Sensitive to heat; keep out of direct sun

Miniature donkey.summary: A small, gentle and affectionate donkey, kept as a companion or for light work.
Miniature donkey.adultSize: Up to about 90 cm at the shoulder, 100–200 kg
Miniature donkey.needs: Grazing or hay, shelter and hoof trimming every 6–10 weeks
Miniature donkey.goodToKnow: Should not be kept alone; does best with another donkey

Boer goat.summary: A hardy, fast-growing meat goat that handles hot climates well.
Boer goat.adultSize: Large; does about 50–80 kg, bucks heavier
Boer goat.needs: Grazing and browsing, shelter, deworming and hoof care
Boer goat.goodToKnow: Good mothers and easy to keep in small herds

Village chicken.summary: A hardy local free-range chicken, kept for eggs and meat.
Village chicken.adultSize: Small; hens about 1–1.5 kg, cocks about 2 kg
Village chicken.needs: A secure coop at night, space to scratch and Newcastle disease vaccines
Village chicken.goodToKnow: Lays fewer eggs than commercial layers but costs little to keep
